questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I really enjoy travelling. Meeting new people and learning about their cultures and how different cultures is represented in the personality of individuals from around the world is very exciting. This was one of the main reasons for my interest in leaving Denmark for half a year.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy! University of Leeds has a very elaborate webpage that assists in most aspects. Any circumstances, questions, etc., that requires further help, can easily and quickly be dealt with per email correspondence with the lovely staff.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: First of all, they made sure that I swiftly got to Leeds from Manchester Airport. They had arranged a bus transport for all the international students arriving. Furthermore, they gave each of us the opportunity to apply for further covid assistance including a start food-package and information on how to order food and goods to be delivered.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was really easy! I applied through the university portal. You can only apply for one, and although I did not get my first priority, I was really satisfied with the outcome. They gave me the opportunity to stay in a flat at Oxley Residences - a bit further away from the city than I expected. The area was definitely one of the more pleasant areas, and the nature surrounding it was indeed worth the extra travel time.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The public transportation in Leeds is not efficient - but it is there. If you fancy biking, the school has a bikehub where you can rent a bike for a decent value. I did not seize this opportunity. Rather, I usually went forth and back with public transportation. When this was not available (e.g., during night time), Ubers and taxis are around for reasonable prices.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was done online. The process was easy, but getting your student ID might take you longer than one might expect. A friend of mine did the registration a month before me, but got his student ID several weeks after me. If you want your student ID faster than what their usual delivery time, head down to the student office in the Marjorie and Arnold Ziff Building.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The staff is always available per email, so if you have any questions, do not hesitate to reach out to them. I believe they would be able to assist with almost everything imaginable, and even if they cannot, they will make sure to help you getting the contact information on any other helpful sources.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was successful in the sense that I ended up having the modules I wanted, but they allow you to change modules two weeks into classes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be careful of changing too many modules once classes have started! I did the mistake of changing half of my modules, and thus was behind from the beginning. I was not able to catch up in the end - some might be, but I had other priorities for my stay.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses vary a lot! I had modules that was very difficult, and I had modules where I did not even participate because it was basic. It really depends on what year of the programme the module is offered (i.e., 1-year modules, 2-year modules, 3-year modules).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: First, the lectures and seminars are shorter! They require more self-study compared to UCPH. Most lectures were online, and all seminars were at campus. Seminars were useful if you came prepared.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Advanced Finance
Financial Mathematics: Risk
Programming for the Web
Statistical Methods
Traditional Alcoholic Beverages 
Economic Controversies

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend any students to do the Traditional Alcoholic Beverages. It is a fairly easy but very interesting module allowing you to put in more energy on other modules. In addition, I recommend any persons from any backgrounds to do the Programming for the Web. You learn the basic foundation of programming, and you will use two of the most common languages (Python and Javascript). It is a tough module, so make sure to have a couple of "easy" modules on the side. And make sure not to have 6 modules in total!

I also want to recommend Advanced Finance to anyone with a economic/financial background.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Depending on how social you are, extra costs can run op. That is, if you attend the pubs often, if you fancy daytrips out of leeds, if you go to football games, etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I did not really have to buy any books, which was a surprise to me.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is an endless list of social clubs and societies that students can join. Furthermore, the city in general is characterised by the immense amount of students and activities. Staying in is really difficult!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Seize the opportunities! Join any society of interest! Attend the fresher's events in the beginning! This is probably the best means to meeting new people and kickstarting your social life in Leeds. I recommend attending the fruity events in the beginning! They are usually crowded, drinks are cheap, and you will get to know a lot of people!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go for daytrips! You should visit cities such as York, Manchester, Liverpool, Newcastle, and even London! We went to London for a weekend trip, and later to celebrate New Years Eve.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The Danish and English culture is pretty similar in many examples, thus making it very easy for me to adjust!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Make sure that you use the pub activities during the weeks! Dry Dock has a fun quiz night during Mondays and the Library has a fun quiz night during Sundays. My friend-group went to the same pub every Wednesday night to play pool! I recommend any friend-groups to have similar traditions! Going out on Wednesdays are really popular in Leeds! You will see how crowded it is when you arrive!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not that I recall.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The pub-culture! It differs a lot from anywhere in the world. Unique is the word!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Do not spend to much time doing schoolwork! 

When finding your modules, make sure you have essays or other assessments that are due before examination, so you do not end up having 6 exams in the examination period! 

Socialise as much as you can in the beginning two weeks! Those two weeks are the most important to create a social foundation for yourself to rely on throughout the rest of the term!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The city is definitely safer than what you will read about it online! Getting home during night is always possible with Ubers or taxis, so do not worry about having to walk through questionable parts like Hyde Park.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The social life.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Leaving Leeds, my friends, and my girlfriend.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
